title: Semrush Review 2026: Is the All-in-One SEO Platform Still Worth $139.95/Month?
content:

## Quick Answer

**Semrush is the best all-in-one SEO platform for 2026**, used by over 10 million marketers and trusted by companies like Samsung, Tesla, IBM, and Wix. It tracks 25+ billion keywords, monitors 43+ trillion backlinks, and covers everything from keyword research and competitor analysis to content marketing, PPC advertising, and — new for 2026 — AI visibility tracking across ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Perplexity.

Starting at $139.95/month (or ~$117.33/month billed annually), Semrush isn't cheap. But compared to buying separate tools for SEO ($99+), content marketing ($60+), PPC research ($99+), and social media management ($60+), it often saves $1,500-2,000/year versus building a multi-tool stack.

The 7-day free trial (no credit card required for the Pro plan) lets you run 10 site audits, track 500 keywords, and analyze 5 competitors without paying a cent — enough to see if it fits your workflow before committing.

## Pros and Cons

### Pros

- **Most comprehensive all-in-one SEO platform**: 55+ tools covering keyword research, competitor analysis, site auditing, backlinks, content marketing, PPC, social media, and local SEO — no other platform matches this breadth
- **Largest keyword database on the market**: 25+ billion keywords with AI-powered intent classification (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational), updated monthly
- **Best-in-class competitor analysis**: .Trends traffic analytics estimates competitor traffic within 20-30% accuracy, reveals their top pages and keywords, and visualizes market share shifts over time
- **Industry-leading PPC intelligence**: Advertising Toolkit reveals competitors' ad copy, landing pages, keyword bids, and budget estimates — a feature Ahrefs and Moz can't match
- **2026 AI innovation**: Copilot delivers personalized, proactive insights from your data; the AI Visibility Toolkit tracks your brand's presence in ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity — a first-of-its-kind feature
- **7-day free trial with no credit card required**: Fully functional Pro plan access including site audits, keyword research, and competitor analysis — genuine risk-free testing
- **Semrush Academy certified training**: Free certification courses in SEO, content marketing, PPC, and social media — recognized by employers and LinkedIn
- **Frequent updates**: 10+ major feature releases in 2026 alone including AI Visibility, Sensor improvements, and ContentShake AI enhancements

### Cons

- **Expensive at higher tiers**: Business plan at $499.95/month is out of reach for most small businesses and solo operators. The jump from Guru ($249.95) to Business nearly doubles the price for features most users don't need
- **Steep learning curve**: The interface has 55+ tools across 10+ toolkits. New users report 2-3 months to achieve basic proficiency, and 6+ months to master the platform — this is a marathon, not a sprint
- **Backlink index lags behind Ahrefs**: At 43 trillion backlinks vs. Ahrefs' 48 trillion, Semrush's index updates slower (every 15-30 days vs. Ahrefs' near real-time). Link builders who need fresh backlink data daily will feel this gap
- **Traffic estimates are approximations, not truth**: .Trends traffic data can be off by 50%+ for sites under 50K monthly visits. Use it directionally — Google Search Console and Google Analytics remain the only sources of truth for your own traffic
- **Social media tools feel bolted on**: The Social Media Toolkit ($60/month extra) lacks the depth of dedicated tools like Buffer or Hootsuite. It's useful for basic scheduling but not a replacement for a specialized social media platform
- **Free plan is essentially a demo**: Limited to 10 requests per day, basic reports only. Competitors like Ahrefs offer genuinely useful free tools (Webmaster Tools, free backlink checker, free keyword generator)

## Who Is Semrush For?

### Ideal Users

- **SEO agencies managing 5+ clients**: Guru and Business plans with client reporting, multi-brand management, and white-label PDFs make Semrush the industry standard for agencies
- **In-house SEO teams at mid-size companies**: The all-in-one nature eliminates tool sprawl — one platform for SEO, content, and competitive intelligence
- **PPC specialists**: No other SEO tool matches Semrush's advertising research — competitor ad history, display network data, and budget estimates are unique differentiators
- **Content marketing teams**: ContentShake AI + SEO Writing Assistant + topic research creates a complete content workflow from ideation to publication
- **SEO consultants and freelancers**: Pro plan ($139.95/month) provides enough firepower for solo practitioners managing up to 5 projects with 500 tracked keywords
- **Companies tracking AI visibility**: The 2026 AI Visibility Toolkit is the only tool that monitors your brand's presence across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity — essential as AI search grows

### Who Should Look Elsewhere

- **Beginners with limited budgets**: If $139.95/month stretches your budget, SE Ranking ($55/month) or Moz Pro ($49/month) provide 85% of the core functionality at 35% of the cost
- **Pure backlink researchers**: If 90% of your work is link building, Ahrefs ($129/month) has a fresher, larger backlink index and faster updates
- **One-person blogs under 10K monthly visits**: Google Search Console + free Ahrefs Webmaster Tools + a budget keyword tool like Keyword Chef or LowFruits covers your needs for $0-25/month
- **Solely social media managers**: Semrush's social tools are supplementary; dedicated platforms like Sprout Social or Hootsuite serve this use case better
- **Enterprise with 50+ users**: BrightEdge or Conductor offer dedicated enterprise features (dedicated account management, custom integrations, enterprise SLA) that Semrush's Business plan doesn't match

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### Keyword Research: The Core of Semrush

Semrush's keyword database has grown to 25+ billion keywords across 140+ country databases, making it the largest commercially available keyword index in 2026.

The **Keyword Magic Tool** is the centerpiece. Enter a seed keyword (e.g., "project management software"), and it generates 20,000-100,000 related keywords grouped by topic clusters. Each keyword shows search volume, trend data (12-month), keyword difficulty (KD%), search intent (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational), CPC, and competitive density.

The AI-powered **intent classification** is particularly valuable — it tells you not just how many people search for a term, but *why* they're searching. This lets you match content types to search intent: informational queries get blog posts and guides, commercial queries get comparison articles and reviews, and transactional queries get landing pages.

**Keyword Gap Analysis** compares your domain against up to 4 competitors simultaneously, identifying keywords they rank for that you don't. It categorizes gaps as "Missing" (competitor ranks, you don't), "Weak" (you rank below position 20), "Strong" (you rank well — opportunities to protect), and "Shared" (both rank — monitor for changes).

**Keyword Overview** provides a single-page snapshot: monthly volume, trend graph, KD%, SERP features (featured snippets, video carousels, knowledge panels, local packs), top-ranking URLs with their backlink counts, and related questions (PAA data extracted from Google's "People Also Ask").

**Practical example**: A SaaS company targeting "best CRM software" in the Keyword Magic Tool discovers 42,000+ related terms including high-value long-tail gems like "best CRM for real estate agents" (2,900 searches/month, KD 45) and "simple CRM for freelancers" (5,400 searches/month, KD 38). These specific queries have lower competition than the head term and higher conversion intent.

### Competitor Analysis: Know Your Market

Semrush's **Domain Analytics** suite reveals competitors' entire SEO and PPC strategies — their top organic keywords, paid keywords, traffic estimates, backlink profiles, and content performance.

**.Trends Traffic Analytics** (new AI-enhanced for 2026) estimates any domain's monthly visits, unique visitors, pages per visit, average visit duration, and bounce rate. It reveals traffic sources (direct, referral, search, social, paid) and audience overlap between domains. The AI models predict traffic trends 3-6 months forward based on historical patterns and algorithm changes.

**Organic Research** shows every keyword a competitor ranks for in the top 100 positions, complete with position tracking over time, estimated traffic per keyword, and SERP feature presence. Filter by position (1-3, 4-10, 11-20), search intent, or traffic potential.

**Traffic Journey** maps the path users take from first search to conversion — which pages they visit, in what order, and which exit pages lose them. This reveals content gaps in the funnel that competitors fill but you don't.

**Market Explorer** analyzes entire industries — total addressable market size, market share distribution, growth trends, seasonality patterns, and emerging players. A SaaS company entering the CRM space can see that the market grew 18% year-over-year but is consolidating around 5 dominant players.

### Site Auditing: Technical SEO at Scale

The **Site Audit** tool crawls your entire website (up to 100,000 pages on Pro, 300,000 on Guru, 1 million on Business) and checks for 140+ technical SEO issues.

Issues are categorized by severity:
- **Errors (red)**: Critical problems that actively hurt rankings — broken links, 404 pages, noindex tags on important pages, duplicate title tags, slow page speed (<40 LCP score)
- **Warnings (orange)**: Medium-impact issues — missing alt text, long meta descriptions, redirect chains, orphaned pages
- **Notices (blue)**: Low-priority optimization opportunities — short content pages, temporary redirects, hreflang inconsistencies

The AI-powered **Issue Prioritization** feature uses machine learning to calculate the actual ranking impact of each issue. Instead of showing a flat list of 500 problems, it identifies the 10-15 fixes that will move the needle most. This is a game-changer for teams drowning in audit reports — fix what matters, don't waste time on cosmetic issues.

**Crawl Comparison** tracks audit scores over time, showing whether your technical health is improving or degrading. Configure the tool to run weekly automatically and receive email digests of new issues.

**Core Web Vitals tracking** monitors LCP, INP, and CLS across all pages, complete with historical trends and page-level breakdowns. The integration with Google's CrUX data lets you compare your lab data with real-user field data.

### Content Marketing & AI Tools

Semrush's content ecosystem has four main pillars for 2026:

**ContentShake AI**: Generate SEO-optimized blog posts from a single keyword or topic. The AI creates an outline, writes the draft with target keywords seeded in, suggests images, and scores readability. Available at different tiers (limited on Pro, standard on Guru, full on Business). The quality is solid for first drafts but always requires human editing for factual accuracy, brand voice, and depth.

**SEO Writing Assistant (SWA)**: Real-time content scoring as you write in Google Docs, WordPress, or Semrush's web editor. Scores on four dimensions: readability (Flesch-Kincaid, sentence length), SEO (keyword usage, title optimization, meta description), tone of voice (formal, casual, neutral), and originality (plagiarism detection). Target scores update dynamically based on top-10 ranking pages for your target keyword — you're optimizing against what's actually working.

**Topic Research**: Enter a broad topic and receive a mind map of subtopics, trending questions, related searches, and headline suggestions. Each subtopic card shows search volume, difficulty, and topic efficiency (a proprietary metric balancing search volume against competition). Use it to build complete content clusters — pillar page + 15-20 supporting articles — that establish topical authority.

**SEO Content Template**: Generates a blueprint for a target keyword: recommended word count, semantically related keywords to include, backlink targets (pages likely to link to this content), readability targets, and SERP analysis showing what Google's currently rewarding for the query.

### AI Visibility Toolkit (New for 2026)

This is Semrush's most forward-looking feature. As AI-powered search engines (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude) shift how users find information, traditional rank tracking becomes insufficient.

The AI Visibility Toolkit:
- Tracks your brand mentions across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity
- Maps custom prompt queries to your brand and category
- Provides an AI Visibility Score that tracks over time
- Identifies which AI models cite your content vs. competitors'
- Reveals the topics and questions where AI search engines recommend your brand

For companies whose traffic increasingly comes from AI search rather than traditional Google — a trend accelerating rapidly in 2026 — this toolkit provides visibility data that no other platform offers. It's included in the Semrush One plan ($199/month).

### PPC & Advertising Intelligence

The **Advertising Toolkit** is arguably Semrush's stealth superpower — no other SEO platform comes close to its PPC research capabilities.

**Advertising Research**: See any competitor's Google Ads history — every ad they've run, landing pages, keywords they bid on, estimated monthly budget, and ad position distribution. Filter by country, device, and date range. You can trace a competitor's PPC strategy over 12 months of historical data.

**PLA Research (Product Listing Ads)**: For ecommerce, see competitors' Google Shopping ads — product titles, images, prices, merchant names, and which keywords trigger their PLAs. Essential competitive intelligence for online retailers.

**Display Advertising**: Track competitors' Google Display Network campaigns — banner creatives, placements, publishers, and estimated impressions. Identify high-performing publisher sites before competitors saturate them.

**Keyword Magic Tool for PPC**: The same keyword database filters for paid metrics — CPC ranges, competitive density, and ad history. Find low-competition, high-conversion paid keywords competitors haven't discovered.

### Breakeven Math

At $139.95/month (Pro plan), Semrush needs to generate $1,679.40/year in value to break even. This could mean:

For agencies, the math is straightforward: one additional client from better competitive intelligence more than covers the annual cost. For in-house teams, the value comes from reduced tool spend and improved SEO performance.

## How to Choose the Right SEO Tool: Buyer's Guide

Choosing an SEO platform is a major investment — you're committing $1,700-6,000/year and 2-3 months of learning time. Here's how to match the tool to your situation.

**Define your primary need first.** If your workflow is 80% link building and backlink analysis, Ahrefs' fresher index (updated daily vs. Semrush's 15-30 days) and larger database (48T vs. 43T) make it the better fit. If you split time between SEO, content, and PPC, Semrush's all-in-one approach eliminates tool sprawl. If you're budget-constrained and need core SEO only, SE Ranking ($55/month) or Moz Pro ($49/month) cover 85% of essential features.

**Consider the learning curve honestly.** Semrush's power comes at the cost of complexity. Budget 10-15 hours in your first month for onboarding (Semrush Academy courses are free and excellent). If you need results in 2 weeks, a simpler tool will get you there faster even if it lacks advanced features.

**Evaluate the free trial thoroughly.** Semrush's 7-day trial (no credit card required for Pro) is genuinely useful — run 2-3 site audits, import your top 50 keywords, analyze 3 competitors, and generate 5 content briefs. This gives you enough data to decide if the workflow fits.

**Check integration requirements.** Semrush integrates with Google Search Console, Google Analytics, Google Ads, Google My Business, and Zapier (connecting to 2,000+ apps). If your team relies on a specific CMS, CRM, or reporting tool, verify the integration exists before committing.

**Factor in team training costs.** A mid-size company with 5 SEO team members investing in Semrush should budget $500-1,000 for team training (courses, workshops, initial consulting) on top of the software cost. The 2-3 month proficiency timeline applies to each team member independently.

**Consider future needs.** If AI visibility tracking matters to your 2026-2027 strategy, no other tool offers what Semrush's AI Visibility Toolkit provides. If you're expanding into PPC, Semrush's Advertising Toolkit saves buying a separate PPC intelligence tool. Invest in the platform that matches your 18-month roadmap, not just your current state.

## Competitor Comparisons

### Semrush vs Ahrefs

The classic debate. Both are excellent — the choice depends on your primary use case.

| Feature | Semrush | Ahrefs |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Starting price | $139.95/mo | $129/mo |
| Keywords tracked | 25B+ | ~20B |
| Backlink index (freshness) | 43T (15-30 day delay) | 48T (near real-time) |
| PPC/advertising research | Industry-best | Very limited |
| Content marketing tools | Built-in platform | Not included |
| Social media tools | Add-on ($60/mo) | Not available |
| AI visibility tracking | Yes (2026) | No |
| Free trial | 7 days, no CC | $7 for 7 days |
| Best for | All-in-one SEO+content+PPC | Backlink analysis, pure SEO |

**Verdict**: Semrush wins for most users because of its breadth. Ahrefs wins for backlink-focused workflows. If you do SEO + content marketing + PPC, Semrush saves $150-300/month versus buying separate tools.

### Semrush vs Moz Pro

Moz Pro ($49/month starting) is much cheaper but significantly less powerful. Moz's keyword database is smaller (approximately 1.25 billion vs. Semrush's 25 billion), its competitor analysis is more basic, and it lacks PPC tools entirely.

Moz's strengths: simpler interface (easier learning curve), excellent beginner education (Moz Academy), and strong local SEO features. Domain Authority (DA) remains the most widely referenced authority metric despite its limitations.

Choose Moz if you're a beginner under $100/month budget. Choose Semrush if you need competitive intelligence, content tools, or PPC data.

### Semrush vs SE Ranking

SE Ranking ($55/month) is the best value-for-money alternative. It covers core SEO needs — keyword rank tracking, website audit, backlink monitoring, and competitor research — at roughly 40% of Semrush Pro's price.

Where SE Ranking falls short: smaller keyword database, less sophisticated competitor analysis, no PPC research, no AI visibility tracking. Where it shines: white-label reports for agencies, included content marketing tools at the base price, and genuinely responsive customer support (G2 rating 4.8/5 vs. Semrush's 4.5/5).

SE Ranking is the best choice for budget-conscious agencies doing white-label work. Semrush is the better choice for competitive intelligence and all-in-one platform needs.

### Semrush vs SpyFu

SpyFu ($39/month) focuses narrowly on competitor keyword research — both SEO and PPC. It's excellent for quickly seeing any domain's most valuable keywords, ad history, and ranking changes. Its interface is simpler and reports generate faster than Semrush's.

SpyFu's limitations: smaller database (fewer keywords, especially outside US/UK), no content tools, no backlink analysis beyond basic reports, no site auditing. It's a specialized tool for competitive keyword research, not a platform.

Choose SpyFu if you exclusively do competitor PPC/SEO keyword research on a tight budget. Choose Semrush if you need the full toolkit.

## 7 Expert Tips to Get the Most from Semrush

1. **Start with a project, not the tool list.** Create your first project immediately after signing up — add your domain, connect Google Search Console and Google Analytics, and run the site audit. This surfaces your most critical issues in the first hour instead of wandering through 55+ tools aimlessly.

2. **Set up Position Tracking on day one.** Add your 50-100 most important keywords, select the correct location targeting (city-level if you're local, country-level if national), and configure weekly email reports. This gives you a baseline and alerts you to ranking shifts before they impact traffic.

3. **Use the Keyword Gap tool before creating any content.** For every new article or page, compare your domain against the top-3 ranking competitors for your target keyword. Identify the keywords they rank for that you don't — these are your content gaps. Write to fill those gaps, not to guess what people search for.

4. **Schedule weekly automatic site audits.** Configure the Site Audit to run every Sunday night. Configure email notifications for new errors only (not warnings). On Monday morning, spend 30 minutes fixing the 2-3 highest-priority errors flagged by the AI prioritization algorithm. This prevents technical debt accumulation.

5. **Use .Trends before pitching a new client.** Before an agency pitches a prospect, run their domain through Traffic Analytics and Organic Research. Identify 5 specific ranking opportunities they're missing — this transforms your pitch from generic to data-backed and increases close rates demonstrably.

6. **Build content clusters with Topic Research.** Instead of creating one-off blog posts, use Topic Research to map a complete content cluster: one pillar page (3,000+ words on a broad topic) and 15-20 supporting articles on specific subtopics. Interlink them. Google rewards topical authority, and this approach builds it systematically.

7. **Monitor competitors' new content with Brand Monitoring.** Set up alerts for your top 5 competitors' brand names and product names. When they publish new content, launch new features, or get mentioned in press — you'll know within hours. React by creating better, more comprehensive content on the same topic.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Semrush worth $139.95 per month?

For most SEO professionals, agencies, and mid-size companies, yes. One additional client acquired through competitive intelligence covers the annual cost ($1,679.40). For solo bloggers under 10K monthly visits, no — free tools (Google Search Console, Ahrefs Webmaster Tools) plus a budget keyword tool ($10-25/month) provide sufficient data at minimal cost.

### Does Semrush offer a free trial?

Yes. Semrush offers a 7-day free trial for the Pro plan with no credit card required. You get full access to core tools including keyword research, site audit (up to 100,000 pages), competitor analysis, position tracking (500 keywords), and content tools. The Guru and Business plans require a credit card for their trials.

### How accurate are Semrush's traffic estimates?

Traffic estimates are approximations based on keyword rankings, estimated CTR by position, and machine learning models. Accuracy varies significantly by site size: within 20-30% for large sites (100K+ monthly visits), but can be off by 50-80%+ for sites under 50K monthly visits. Use directionally — never present Semrush traffic estimates to clients as fact. Google Search Console and Google Analytics are the only accurate sources for real traffic data.

### What's the difference between Semrush Pro and Guru?

The main differences: Guru ($249.95/mo) adds 15 projects (vs. 5 on Pro), 1,500 tracked keywords (vs. 500), 2 years of historical data (vs. 1 year), the full Content Marketing Platform, branded PDF reports, multi-location tracking, ContentShake AI access, and extended API limits. Guru is the minimum viable tier for agencies managing multiple clients. Pro is sufficient for in-house SEO teams managing one website.

### Is Semrush better than Ahrefs?

For most users, yes — because of breadth. Semrush covers SEO + content marketing + PPC + social media in one platform. Ahrefs is better for backlink analysis (fresher index, daily updates) and simpler for pure-SEO workflows. If your work is 60%+ link building, Ahrefs wins. If you do SEO plus any combination of content, PPC, or competitive intelligence, Semrush wins by eliminating tool sprawl.

### Can I cancel Semrush anytime?

Yes, Semrush subscriptions can be canceled at any time. Monthly plans stop immediately at the end of the current billing period. Annual plans continue through the end of the committed term — early cancellation of annual plans does not provide a prorated refund. Semrush's refund policy is 7 days from the initial purchase date for first-time subscribers.

### Does Semrush work for local SEO?

Yes, but you need the Local SEO add-on ($30-60/month) for full local functionality. Core features useful for local SEO include: local keyword research (city + service combinations), Google Business Profile audit and listing management, local rank tracking (ZIP code or city-level), review monitoring across Google, Yelp, and Facebook, and local competitor analysis. The Local SEO Toolkit specifically handles NAP consistency, citation building, and GBP optimization.

### What is Semrush One?

Semrush One ($199/month) is a 2026 bundle that combines the Pro-tier SEO tools with the new AI Visibility Toolkit. It's designed for brands that want traditional SEO capabilities plus tracking of their presence in AI search engines (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity). The AI Visibility Toolkit is not available separately at a published price; Semrush One is currently the only way to access it below Enterprise tier.

### How many keywords can I track in Semrush?

Pro plan tracks 500 keywords, Guru tracks 1,500, and Business tracks 5,000. Keywords are checked daily, weekly, or on-demand based on your settings. Position Tracking supports desktop and mobile, multiple locations per keyword, and local (city-level) and national tracking. You can add more tracked keywords for an additional fee on any plan.

### Does Semrush have an affiliate program?

Yes. Semrush runs an affiliate program through the Impact network paying 40% commission on first sales and 10-30% on recurring subscriptions, with a 120-day cookie window. The program is available to content creators, agencies, and marketing professionals. Payouts process through PayPal or direct deposit with a $50 minimum threshold.

## Final Verdict

Semrush is the undisputed all-in-one SEO champion for 2026. Its combination of the largest keyword database (25B+), industry-best competitor analysis, built-in content marketing tools, unique PPC intelligence, and forward-looking AI visibility tracking makes it the platform that covers the broadest range of marketing needs under a single login.

It is not perfect. The learning curve is real and steep — budget 2-3 months to reach proficiency. The pricing at higher tiers ($499.95/month for Business) excludes small businesses and solo operators. Backlink freshness lags behind Ahrefs, and traffic estimates for small sites are unreliable.

But for the target audience — SEO agencies, in-house marketing teams at mid-size companies, PPC specialists, and content marketers — Semrush delivers more value per dollar than any single competitor. One platform replacing 3-4 separate tools saves $1,500-2,000/year in subscription costs while reducing tool-switching friction.

**The bottom line**: If you can afford the $139.95/month entry price and commit to the learning curve, no other SEO platform matches Semrush's breadth, innovation pace, or competitive intelligence depth. mainEntity.name: Does Semrush offer a free trial?

mainEntity.name: How accurate are Semrush's traffic estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traffic estimates are approximations based on keyword rankings, estimated CTR by position, and machine learning models. Accuracy varies significantly by site size: within 20-30% for large sites (100K+ monthly visits), but can be off by 50-80%+ for sites under 50K monthly visits. Use directionally — never present Semrush traffic estimates to clients as fact. Google Search Console and Google Analytics are the only accurate sources for real traffic data.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Semrush Pro and Guru?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main differences: Guru ($249.95/mo) adds 15 projects (vs. 5 on Pro), 1,500 tracked keywords (vs. 500), 2 years of historical data (vs. 1 year), the full Content Marketing Platform, branded PDF reports, multi-location tracking, ContentShake AI access, and extended API limits. Guru is the minimum viable tier for agencies managing multiple clients. Pro is sufficient for in-house SEO teams managing one website.

mainEntity.name: Does Semrush work for local SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but you need the Local SEO add-on ($30-60/month) for full local functionality. Core features useful for local SEO include: local keyword research (city + service combinations), Google Business Profile audit and listing management, local rank tracking (ZIP code or city-level), review monitoring across Google, Yelp, and Facebook, and local competitor analysis. The Local SEO Toolkit specifically handles NAP consistency, citation building, and GBP optimization.

mainEntity.name: How many keywords can I track in Semrush?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pro plan tracks 500 keywords, Guru tracks 1,500, and Business tracks 5,000. Keywords are checked daily, weekly, or on-demand based on your settings.
